name: Brundarok
text: Bronze rail. Carts ride it up to 0.6 blocks per tick, half again vanilla speed. Curves, slopes and junctions work like a normal rail. Age III.

name: Brundavoss
text: Bronze powered rail. Boosts a cart when powered, stops it when not. Caps at 0.6 blocks per tick. Age III.

name: Sorvanquil
text: Steel rail. Carts ride it up to 0.9 blocks per tick, more than twice vanilla speed. Age V.

name: Sorvaleth
text: Steel powered rail. A stronger boost than bronze, same stop when unpowered. Caps at 0.9 blocks per tick. Age V.

name: Zephrakund
text: High-speed rail. Carts ride it up to 1.2 blocks per tick, three times vanilla speed. Keep curves gentle. Age VI.

name: Zephravoss
text: High-speed powered rail. The strongest boost, caps at 1.2 blocks per tick. Age VI.

name: Haldurmek
text: Station rail. Stops a cart that rolls onto it and holds it until the rail is powered, or until its timer ends. Use it bare-handed to cycle the timer: signal only, 2, 5, 15 or 60 seconds. A coupled follower follows its leader instead. Age V.

name: Eskavorn
text: One-way rail. A steel-speed rail with an arrow, set to the way you face when you place it. A cart rolling against the arrow is stopped dead; carts going with it pass as on any rail. Place it straight, on a flat run. Age V.

name: Tarvelmok
text: Destination rail. A steel-speed detector rail with a coloured bar. Label a cart by using a dye on it (sneak with an empty hand to wipe the label); use a dye on the rail to choose which label it reads, an empty hand to make it read every cart. It gives a redstone signal only while a cart with a matching label is on it, so a row of them sorts a mixed line: wire each to a powered rail or junction. Age V.

name: Voskarmeth
text: Cart loader. Put its back against a chest, barrel or hopper and its front toward a rail: it moves items between that container and a container cart (chest, hopper) standing on the rail, a stack every 8 ticks. Use it bare-handed to switch between loading and unloading; a redstone signal switches it off. Age V.

name: Hardemvoss
text: Rail yard controller. Choose a freight or bulk yard bare-handed (sneak to change), install cart chassis, two wheelsets and a body in that order by using them on it, and it builds each stage by itself. Bare-handed once complete it rolls a coupled train of three carts onto a rail within 3 blocks; with no rail nothing is spent. Parts need Age III. A real-time block, no turns.

name: Fremvak
text: Cart chassis. First part of a yard build: the frame the wheelsets and the body go on. Age III.

name: Rotamvek
text: Wheelset. Two go on each cart after the chassis. Age III.

name: Grathmark
text: Freight body. The last part of a freight build: three chest carts roll out. Age III.

name: Skarvund
text: Bulk body. The last part of a bulk build: three hopper carts roll out. Age III.

name: Quelvarith
text: Coupling chain. Use it on one cart, then on a second: the first leads, the second follows at a fixed spacing and is pulled along, so a row of carts runs as a train. A link breaks if the carts get more than 8 blocks apart. Age V.

name: Snithrekel
text: Chain cutters. Sneak and use on a cart to cut its link and get the chain back. Age V.
